text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Funds from deposits levied on imports of selected consumer goods will be channelled from commercial banks to the central bank through the state-run Konsolidacna Banka.
- The Finance Ministry and the central bank will, within two months, work out a proposal on the use the import deposits.
- Slovakia's largest commercial bank, VUB, plans to open a branch in Moscow and a representative office in Shanghai. VUB on Tuesday opened a representative office in the London City.
- Property worth some 30 billion crowns remains to be privatised to complete the privatisation process in Slovakia.
- Agriculture Minister Peter Baco said Slovakia would probably impose import quotas on Czech beer.

PRAVDA - The Slovak government and the NBS have rejected demands by the Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) to introduce the payment of a 13th salary each year, saying the country's economy could not afford it.
- KOZ said it would stick to its demand for a 13th salary since this was demanded by all trade unions members.
- The standard of living in Slovakia has decreased by about 30 percent from levels before the revolution of 1989.
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka, the former Czechoslovak foreign trade bank, has taken Slovakia to the arbitrage court in Washington for failing to repay debts worth some 13 billion crowns.
- The opposition Democratic Union (DU) has called on other opposition parties to form a joint shadow government.
SME - President Michal Kovac has started a campaign to regulary inform citizens about his opinions on public matters, such as NATO membership and direct presidential elections.
- The average monthly salary is expected to increase to some 9,000 crowns in 1997, from 8,154 crowns in 1996.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The European Union has criticised a recent Slovak measure imposing 20 percent deposits on imports of selected consumer goods from all countries.
